blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935, under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
The setup of the central bank was based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926).
Originally established as a private shareholders' bank, the RBI was fully nationalised on January 1, 1949.
The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 provides the comprehensive legal framework for the regulation and supervision of commercial banking institutions in India.
Frequently tested: Hilton Young Commission (1926) recommended the setup of RBI.
Distinguish clearly between the RBI Act, 1934 (monetary authority framework) and the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (bank licensing and operational control).
RBI was nationalised under the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948, taking effect on January 1, 1949.
